Management further signaled that price increases were becoming effective, contributing to the regaining of margin percentages, despite ongoing pressures from increased raw material costs due to tariffs. The backlog also grew 9.7% to $166.6 million from the end of the previous quarter and 125% from the prior year, with management signaling expectations for continued gross margin recovery as production increases and the company works through its backlog, which is benefiting from escalating value due to multiple price increases, including a new 5% increase announced for early June.
